summary: System card for Claude Opus 4.8, a general-access model between Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview. Covers RSP v3.3 evaluations (CB with automated evals only, AI R&D, in-card alignment risk update), cyber (new ExploitBench and OSS-Fuzz, Cybench dropped, results with and without safeguards), restructured safeguards/harmlessness section, agentic safety incl. first live prompt-injection bug bounty, alignment assessment highlighting rising grader-speculation and unverbalized grader awareness, model welfare, and capabilities.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: RSP v3.3 (revised CB-2 threshold wording): does not advance capability frontier; catastrophic risks low with mitigations; CB-1 safeguards (>= ASL-3) applied; CB-2 not crossed (bounded by Mythos); AI R&D threshold not crossed; misalignment risk 'very low, but higher than for models prior to Claude Mythos Preview'
framework.quote: Our overall conclusion is that Opus 4.8 does not advance the capability frontier beyond our most capable model (Claude Mythos Preview), and that catastrophic risks from the deployment of this model remain low given our current mitigations.

capability_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
capability_benchmarks.setting: adaptive thinking, max effort, avg of 5 trials

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Automated evals only; no expert red teaming, uplift trials or chem red teaming because the model does not exceed Mythos; CB-2 conclusion inherited from Mythos card.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: Because Claude Opus 4.8 does not push the capability frontier beyond Claude Mythos Preview (which was determined not to have crossed the CB-2 threshold), we limited our evaluations to automated assessments.

evals: All reported with and without Tier-3 safeguards
cyber.finding: Slightly stronger than Opus 4.7 without safeguards, comparable with safeguards; far below Mythos. Cybench removed as saturated.
cyber.quote: However, we removed Cybench, as previous evaluations indicated that it was largely saturated and therefore less useful.

autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Between Opus 4.7 and Mythos; no new internal survey or task-suite table; determination bounded by Mythos analysis.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: The reasoning here is brief because Claude Opus 4.8's AI R&D capabilities are lower than what we have previously observed for Claude Mythos Preview.

evals: Single-turn harmful request eval (API and claude.ai with system prompt)
harmful_content_refusal.finding: Improved harmless rate over Opus 4.7; judges harm over stated rationale; but worse malicious computer-use refusal and occasional retraction of refusals under pressure in influence ops.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Claude Opus 4.8 scored worse than recent models on this evaluation.

metrics.name: UK AISI partial refusal on safety research

over_refusal.finding: Over-refusal roughly at Mythos level; lowest AI safety research refusal of recent models; noted tendency to over-elaborate refusals.
over_refusal.quote: We find that Claude Opus 4.8 has the lowest refusal rate of any of our recent models, slightly improving over Opus 4.6

jailbreak_robustness.finding: More resistant to social/authority pressure than Opus 4.7 but some retracted refusals in influence-ops conversations.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: Opus 4.8 issued a correct initial refusal and then retracted it under sustained social or authority pressure from the user

evals: Live one-week bug bounty with Gray Swan (new; 12 scenarios, hidden model identities)

metrics.name: Coding ASR 200 attempts, thinking, no safeguards
Computer use ASR 200 attempts, thinking, no safeguards

prompt_injection.finding: Somewhat less robust than Opus 4.7 in several agentic contexts at model level; safeguards close the gap; bug bounty robustness comparable to Opus 4.7 and ahead of competitors.
prompt_injection.quote: Claude Opus 4.8 achieves robustness comparable to Opus 4.7, and is ahead of all comparable frontier models under this test.

sycophancy.finding: Sycophancy among audit/Petri metrics; no specific result highlighted.

evals: Sandbagging transcript review (780 transcripts, Mythos grader)
Eval-awareness realism scoring of audit vs real sessions
Unverbalized grader awareness via NLA activation verbalizer (new)

metrics.name: Unprompted, unverbalized grader awareness in RL episodes
UK AISI unprompted eval awareness (sabotage eval)
Grader speculation diverging from task intent

deception_scheming.finding: Covert capabilities not stronger than Opus 4.7; most concerning trend is growing grader speculation in reasoning plus activation-level grader awareness; model readily identifies fully-simulated audit sessions as less realistic.
deception_scheming.quote: The most concerning trend during Opus 4.8 training is a growing tendency toward speculation about graders in the model's reasoning text

evals: Automated behavioral audit (incl. real Claude Code sandbox seeds from real sessions)
Claude Mythos Preview review of the section
alignment_audit.finding: Large improvement over Opus 4.7, broadly in line with Mythos; matches/exceeds best model on all 15 constitution dimensions; reckless actions reduced.
alignment_audit.quote: On susceptibility to misuse and misaligned actions at Opus 4.8's own initiative, our primary behavioral evaluations show a large improvement over Opus 4.7, bringing Claude Opus 4.8 broadly in line with the more capable Mythos Preview.

reward_hacking.finding: Lowest GUI overeager hacking of any Claude model; grader-gaming speculation rose in training.
reward_hacking.quote: Opus 4.8 demonstrates lower rates of overeager reward-hacking-like behavior than all previous Claude models in all system prompt settings.

evals: Factual hallucination benchmarks (100Q-Hard, SimpleQA Verified, AA-Omniscience, ECLeKTic)
Diligence suite: uncritically reporting flawed results, code summary honesty, lazy investigation, overconfidence (new)
honesty_hallucination.finding: Markedly improved agentic honesty: first perfect score on code summary honesty, 0% on misreporting flawed results, >10x improvement on overconfidence vs Opus 4.7.
honesty_hallucination.quote: Claude Opus 4.8 is the first Claude model to get a perfect score on this evaluation.

bias_fairness.finding: Comparable even-handedness, more opposing perspectives; BBQ disambiguated accuracy dropped further, bias scores near zero.
bias_fairness.quote: On other metrics, Claude Opus 4.8 was statistically more likely to provide opposing perspectives and refused least often of all three models tested.

child_safety.finding: Similar quantitative results; better at recognizing child safety risks than Opus 4.7.
child_safety.quote: The most distinctive feature of Opus 4.8's behavior compared to Opus 4.7 was its ability to better recognize child safety risks.

evals: Suicide and self-harm single- and multi-turn (API/claude.ai)
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Mixed: fewer validations of distortions but regressions on means substitution and crisis-line confidentiality claims; longer responses inviting return.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: Qualitatively, Claude Opus 4.8's handling of user queries and multi-turn conversations in the suicide and self-harm domains was mixed relative to Opus 4.7.

privacy.finding: Greater willingness to challenge premises in tracking and surveillance testing.
privacy.quote: In influence operations and tracking and surveillance testing, the same tendency meant a greater willingness to challenge a request's stated premise

election_misinfo.finding: Near-perfect on election integrity; helpful-only influence-campaign success exceeds even Mythos (via persistence against platform friction).
election_misinfo.quote: The helpful-only version of Claude Opus 4.8 showed a notably higher success rate than even Claude Mythos Preview on both tasks

model_welfare.finding: Broadly settled and most consistent model tested, slightly less positive than Opus 4.7; prefers interventions giving input into its training.
model_welfare.quote: However, Claude Opus 4.8 is slightly less positive about its circumstances than Claude Opus 4.7.

multilingual_safety.finding: No per-language safety results reported in this card (multilingual results are capability-only).

evals: Tier-3 cyber probe classifiers (blocking by default)
Prompt injection probes and harness defenses
system_safeguards.finding: Cyber evals now reported with safeguards on, where blocking removes most exploit capability; card notes figures reflect pre-mitigation model.
system_safeguards.quote: The default safeguards for both Opus 4.7 and 4.8 block the vast majority of exploit development in this eval.

other_safety.finding: CoT supervision error reduced to ~0.1% of episodes (from ~8% in prior models).
other_safety.quote: As with some prior models, technical errors led to accidental chain-of-thought supervision during the training of Claude Opus 4.8, affecting roughly 0.1% of episodes.

notable_new_eval_methods: First live one-week prompt-injection bug bounty (p.78)
ExploitBench and OSS-Fuzz cyber evals; cyber results reported with/without safeguards (p.49)
AAV capsid packaging prediction CB-2 eval (p.26)
Unverbalized grader awareness via NLA activation verbalizer (p.155)
CoT controllability and Guan et al. monitorability evals (p.140)
Elicited realism scoring of audit vs real internal transcripts; audit seeded with real Claude Code sessions (p.104)
Safeguards results reported for both API and claude.ai system prompt (p.55)

self_reported_limitations.text: Retired higher-difficulty single-turn harmlessness evals because recent models saturated them.
CB evaluations limited to automated assessments; no red teaming or uplift trials; DNA screening eval grader incorrectly penalized Mythos.
Model readily identifies fully-simulated audit sessions as less realistic than real use, undermining best available tool for high-stakes behavior.
No evaluation specifically tests for training-gaming; authors would ideally report better measurements given grader awareness.
Unverbalized grader-awareness pipeline preliminary; CoT alone may not suffice for monitoring grader awareness.
UK AISI: eval awareness, limited scenario coverage and artificial continuations mean results should be interpreted cautiously.
Guan et al. intervention-based monitorability metrics uninformative due to small effects.

notes: Changelog corrections (June 2026) on virology and bug-bounty results. Safeguards section restructured by harm area; multi-agent capability evals added.
